newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up on oversold signals, soymeal.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up on oversold signals, soymeal.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on short covering tied to signals the market was oversold and to a strong tone in nearby soymeal because of commercial buying, traders said.
Fund buying led the way up but a rally was flattened near the close on late local selling, they said.
"They (locals) bought it all day and late in the day they turned to the sell side," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Traders said the soybean market was due for a bounce after the market began tumbling in mid-July.

Nearby November soybeans set a contract high of $8.25 per bushel on July 12. But since then the market has fallen roughly $1.65 per bushel, a 20 percent loss in value. November touched a harvest low of $6.59-3/4 Friday which also was an 11-1/2 month low. The session low Monday was $6.60.
Short term indicators show the market oversold with November's nine day relative strength index (RSI) on a daily basis closing at 23.5 points. An RSI of 30 or less is considered an oversold market.
Soybeans closed one to five cents per bushel higher, with November up 2-3/4 at $6.66.
But the key moving averages show the market remains bearish over the longer term.

"Everybody was a little spooked into short covering but the close wasn't all that impressive," said Mark Cermak of Chicago-trade house O'Connor and Co. "Exports were good but obviously the market has much broader work to do if it's going to see a turn in direction."
Fundamentals were little changed. But some considered the fact Tenco Inc stopped over one million bushels of the soy posted Monday for delivery on the Nov as mildly bullish.
Slow farmer selling of soybeans and commercial buying in the soymeal pit helped buoy the market as did bullish input from Monday's USDA weekly soybean export inspections tally.
USDA said soybeans inspected for export during the week ended October 31 totaled 28.191 million bushels, at the high end of trade expections for 25 million to 30 million bushels.

Technicians cited first resistance in the November at $6.68-1/4 and second resistance at $6.77-1/2. The session high as of 1145 CST was $6.68-1/2. First support was at $6.59 and second support was $6.49-3/4. The session low for November was $6.60 and the high was $6.71.

Traders also said the market was evening up before the expected release this week of several private crop estimates. Farmers Commodities Corp, Sparks Companies and the Leslie-ADM Elevator Survey area expected to be released to clients this week, the traders said.
"The market is talking about a 9.2 billion corn number and 2.4 billion bushel soybean number," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA's October crop report indicated 1996 U.S. soybean production at 2.346 billion bushels. The November USDA crop report is slated for release on November 12.
Key buyers of futures on the day included Lit America, Merrill Lynch Futures, O'Connor and Co and Dean Witter Reynolds each bought 2.5 million bushels of January, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 65,000, down from 78,564 Friday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Smith Barney bought 2,000 January $6.50 puts and bought 1,500 March $6.50 puts, traders said. Continental Grain bought 600 March $7.50 calls and sold 600 March $7.00 calls at 10-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 18,000, down from 34,833 Friday.
